text:
maya: seeing a bunch of netdev rx errors on east3a-gpu-pool nodes, and GPUs are reporting thermal_clamp events. p95 token latency spiking for inferences routed there :warning:
liam: which AZ exactly? east3a? can you paste node names?
maya: east3a, nodes gpu-e3a-12..18, logs show repeated "thermal_trip: GPU clock throttled to 60%" and kernel net errors 'napi_poll: rx dropped'
jordan-sre: incident-bot created INC-2026-87 for east3a partial degrade (ops-bot) :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: INC-2026-87 created, severity: S2, owner: eng-oncall, runbook: /runbooks/az-thermal-network-degrade
olivia: marking noncritical batch queues as low-priority and preparing to drain them off east3a first. plan: 1) cordon problematic nodes, 2) drain batch pods, 3) route real-time traffic away, 4) evacuate remaining pods gradually. comments?
liam: +1. prefer graceful drain with --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data and set grace-period 120s for model servers. command: kubectl drain gpu-e3a-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
noah: watch out for KV cache cold starts. we should pre-warm caches in target pools before shifting heavy latencies. will spin up a few replicas in usw2 and warm prefix cache.
maya: starting cordon and drain on gpu-e3a-12..15 now. low-priority pods evicting.
ops-bot: scheduler: autoscaler lowering desired for east3a GPU nodegroup by 30% and creating 8 nodes in usw2 as replacement per policy 'zonal-evac-redirect'.
jordan-sre: routing: initiating weight shift in traffic-controller. pseudo: set-route-weight --from east3a --to usw2,usw2b --weights 0.2,0.8 --ramp 5m
liam: confirm model-version pinning: ensure hosted route can fallback to quantized variant if latency rises. updating rollout to add fallback=redwood-quant-v2 for east3a requests.
noah: prewarming done on macs in usw2. pinging health-check endpoint with representative prompts to populate KV cache. results: warm hit rate ~85% after 4m.
maya: observed one node with persistent link flaps (gpu-e3a-17) — NIC hardware errors, opening ticket with cloud provider and tagging node for replacement.
jordan-sre: decision: avoid full AZ evacuation; target affected node subset and shift steady-state traffic. we will keep control plane in east3a but stop scheduling new GPU jobs there until provider confirms NIC replacement.
liam: cost note: spinning up on-demand in usw2 will increase short-term costs ~+18% for the hour, but avoids SLA breaches. filing cost-ops ticket.
ops-bot: deploy-bot scheduled a controlled rollout of routing change. deploy-bot: rollout started, id=rt-1942-01, batch=3 nodes per step
maya: drain complete for 12..15. batch job evictions succeeded, no restarted pods from critical pools yet.
noah: observed some retries from client-side due to route changes, but success rate recovering to 99.2%.
jordan-sre: monitoring: keep an eye on p95 latency and error budget. escalation if p95 > 350ms for more than 10m.
liam: next steps: 1) collector of logs and dmesg for gpu-e3a-17, 2) provider ticket follow-up, 3) leave a small warm standby in east3a for failback, 4) update post-incident notes. assigning tasks in INC-2026-87.
maya: adding logs snippet below for triage:
```
[ 145.732112] GPU0: therm_trip: throttling to 600MHz
[ 145.732130] net_eth0: rx_errors=1324 rx_dropped=78
[ 145.742001] mlx5_core 0000:65:00.0: 6: link down
```
liam: thanks, will attach to incident. folks, if you see more degrading nodes call it out. planning to close the active evacuation window in 40m unless trend worsens. :hourglass: 
noah: noted. I'll keep warming caches and watch token latency dashboards.
ops-bot: incident INC-2026-87 updated: action=partial-az-targeted-drain, status=mitigating
